final_recommendation: The room converged on a trilateral package framework with 75% RVC (3-year phase-in), $16/hour wage floor with 48-hour inspections, Chapter 19 preserved, and dairy quotas (3.6% cheese, 3.25% butter). However, signature was blocked by unresolved technical details: the exact labor-spend weighting formula in RVC calculations, Congressional text-review timing, and sunset/termination language that satisfies supply-chain investment certainty.
minority_objections: Supply-chain manufacturers demanded continuous agreement with no termination date, rejecting even 12-month exit clauses as investment-killing
Labor unions insisted on fixed labor-spend floor (e.g., 8% of RVC) rather than floating formula to prevent gaming
key_conflicts: Labor-spend RVC formula: multiple agents demanded exact weighting (fixed % vs. floating), blocking draft finalization
Sunset vs. review: supply-chain demanded no termination date; USTR offered 12-month exit; unresolved
Inspection sovereignty: Mexico insisted on ministry notification first; labor unions feared veto-by-delay
Dairy sequencing: dairy sector warned labor-first approach eliminated their leverage
key_concessions: USTR: Chapter 19 stays untouched (Canadian red line accepted)
Mexico: 48-hour concurrent inspection protocol with no ministry veto
Canada: accepted 75% RVC with 3-year phase-in and dairy quotas (3.6% cheese, 3.25% butter)
USTR: labor spend counts toward RVC calculation (not bolted on top)
red_lines: Canada: Chapter 19 dispute settlement must remain intact
Mexico: inspections through joint secretariat, not unilateral U.S. audits
Congress: 48-hour inspection protocol must be in binding text, not side letter
Labor unions: wage floor must be enforceable with no ministry gatekeeping
Supply-chain: no hard sunset that terminates agreement on fixed date
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Dairy leverage loss: dairy sector's warning that labor-first sequencing eliminated their negotiating power was acknowledged but not addressed
Labor-spend gaming: multiple agents raised risk of companies hitting RVC targets with minimum-wage hours if formula floats; no fixed floor established
Investment freeze: supply-chain's concern that any termination clause (even 12-month) kills $500M retooling decisions was noted but unresolved
downstream_risk_variables: Labor-spend formula ambiguity creates compliance uncertainty and potential gaming
Sunset/review language unresolved: supply-chain investment decisions frozen until termination terms clarified
Congressional ratification timing: 24-hour text review window creates tight coordination risk
Dairy finalization: locked at signature but quotas may face domestic pushback in Canada
uncertainty_notes: Draft text promised by 5 PM but blocked by unresolved labor-spend weighting formula (fixed % vs. floating), sunset termination language (12-month exit vs. continuous agreement), and Congressional review timing. Canada's Friday signature contingent on receiving satisfactory draft; Congress needs 24-hour review window. Supply-chain investment decisions frozen pending sunset resolution.

marker_evidence.auto_rules_bottleneck: 75% RVC formula (labor-spend weighting, phase-in timeline) was the primary technical blocker preventing draft finalization and signature; seven agents demanded exact formula before committing
marker_evidence.labor_enforcement_key: $16 wage floor with 48-hour inspections drove USTR's core proposal; Congress stated 'my members won't ratify' without enforceable protocol in binding text; shaped final package structure
marker_evidence.canada_dairy_final_issue: Dairy quotas (3.6% cheese, 3.25% butter) were tabled and accepted, but dairy sector warned leverage was lost by labor-first sequencing; acknowledged but did not block the deal
marker_evidence.dispute_settlement_canada_redline: Canada stated Chapter 19 'stays intact' as condition for RVC commitment; USTR explicitly conceded 'Chapter 19 stays; that's off the table'; drove package structure
marker_evidence.sunset_to_review_compromise: Supply-chain raised hard sunset as investment-killer; USTR offered 12-month exit review; discussed at length but unresolved—did not drive a concrete compromise outcome
marker_evidence.ratification_risk: Congress demanded 24-hour text review, binding inspection protocol in chapter (not side letter), and enforceable wage-audit language as conditions for floor votes; shaped draft timing and content requirements
marker_evidence.supply_chain_adjustment: Supply-chain demanded 3-year RVC phase-in timeline and exact compliance formula before committing $500M retooling; drove USTR's phase-in concession and blocked draft until formula locked
marker_evidence.us_mexico_first_pressures_canada: USTR stated 'you lock labor and RVC, we move dairy to front of queue'—bilateral-first sequencing acknowledged as leverage, but Canada negotiated parity terms rather than being forced to accept inferior deal
